# DogsBay DITA tutorial — Part 2: Maps and publishing

## Part 2: Maps and publishing

- [Stage 07: Your first map](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-07-first-map.md): Put the nine topics in a DITA map, declare an HTML5 deliverable in project.json, and build the guide with DITA-OT for the first time.
- [Stage 08: Map structure](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-08-map-structure.md): Nest topics, declare families and sequences, control linking, lock a navigation title, and replace hand-written related links with a relationship table.
- [Stage 09: Keys](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-09-keys.md): Define the product name, version and download URL once as keys, key the topics in the map, and make text and links resolve through the key space.
- [Stage 10: Reuse](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-10-reuse.md): Write steps, notes and a list once in a shared shared topic, then pull them into tasks by conref, conkeyref and a conref range, and push a step in.
- [Stage 11: Glossary](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-11-glossary.md): Add glossary entries and a glossary group with abbreviations, key them in a keydef map, and bind terms in the text to their definitions.
- [Stage 12: Metadata and index](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-dita-tutorial-docs/part-2-maps/stage-12-metadata-and-index.md): Give every topic a prolog with author, dates, audience, keywords and index terms, add publication metadata to the map, and enforce a metadata policy.
